title: Automated Counting of Microglia in Mouse Brain Slices After Immunofluorescence Staining
author: Amandine EVEN

steps.title: Prepare brain sections and stain
steps.instruction: Cut 40 µm coronal mouse brain sections and perform immunohistochemistry using DAPI and Iba1 (additional markers optional).

steps.title: Acquire z‑stack images
steps.instruction: Scan regions of interest in z‑stacks at 1 µm intervals. Use either wide‑field scans at 20× (minimum 15 z‑planes) on a Zeiss AxioScan 7 slide scanner or single‑field confocal images at 40× (minimum 35 z‑planes) on a Nikon Eclipse Ti2.

steps.title: Convert image file format
steps.instruction: If acquired files are not in ND2 format, convert them to TIFF or ND2 before further processing.

steps.title: Train AI segmentation model
steps.instruction: In NIS‑Elements, run a “Segment Objects AI” job on the training images for at least 200 iterations to create a microglial segmentation model.

steps.title: Evaluate and improve segmentation
steps.instruction: Visually assess AI‑generated segmentation masks; if performance is insufficient, add more annotated images and retrain the model until accuracy is acceptable.

steps.title: Manually refine masks
steps.instruction: Open the AI masks in the NIS binary editor, manually correct segmentation errors, and save the corrected images and masks.

steps.title: Integrate model into GA3 workflow
steps.instruction: Add a SegmentObject.ai box to a GA3 pipeline, connect it to an Object Count module, and load the trained AI model for microglial segmentation and counting.

steps.title: Prepare representative images
steps.instruction: Select 10 representative images and apply the same preprocessing (e.g., denoising or deconvolution) required for downstream analysis.

steps.title: Run batch analysis
steps.instruction: Save the GA3 pipeline and execute it in batch mode within NIS‑Elements on the 10 selected images.

steps.title: Verify results with masks
steps.instruction: Open each processed image together with its associated mask; confirm Iba1 signal appears green and the cell‑body mask is displayed in red.
